A1.justification: Despite the changed title and extensive restructuring, both PDFs describe the same informed meta-learning framework and Informed Neural Process (INP). Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original synthetic regression, weather prediction and CUB-200-2011 classification experiments in Section 4, plus robustness analyses in Appendix A.6.

after.justification: v5 retains original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendix A.8 and adds analyses including a Bayesian regression comparison.

M1.justification: The INP encoders, fusion alternatives, latent distribution, decoder, ELBO training and random knowledge masking are retained. v5's worked MAML example elaborates v4's general knowledge-to-meta-parameters construction; the PDFs do not establish a changed underlying INP procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate sinusoidal regression, USCRN temperature prediction and CUB-200-2011 classification, including the same distribution-shift settings. The added analyses use retained coverage. The application domains listed in v5 Table A.2 are prospective examples, not additional evaluations.

E2.justification: v5 Appendix A.8.4 and Figure A.5 add a parametric Bayesian regression comparator with ground-truth functional form and priors, evaluated with and without knowledge. Existing NP comparisons remain. This extends the comparator set within the synthetic regression study.

E3.justification: The new Bayesian comparison fixes the noise and revealed parameters to their true values and includes inference-time measurements. Figure 7b also adds weather evaluation at 15 context points, although the setup still specifies at most 10. Previously reported dataset splits, model configurations and training settings are otherwise retained.

E4.justification: v5 adds error-versus-frequency analysis of generalisation to unseen knowledge values (Figure 5b) and investigates approximation and computational tradeoffs against Bayesian regression (Appendix A.8.4). It replaces v4's parameter-specific and range-averaged uncertainty analyses with direct data-versus-knowledge comparisons (Figure 6). The earlier training-size, knowledge-complexity and spurious-correlation studies remain.

E5.justification: v5 newly identifies the weather and classification standard errors as bootstrap estimates, specifies within-bin standard deviations in Figure 5b, and documents four NUTS chains with burn-in and estimation sample counts for the Bayesian reference. These additions do not establish more repeated INP training runs.

E6.justification: Synthetic learning curves, distribution-shift curves and knowledge-type improvement bars change. Weather zero-shot entries change from 57.7%/48.1% in v4 Table 2 to 63.5%/60.7% in v5 Figure 7b, while its prose retains the old percentages. v5 adds detailed knowledge-type likelihoods and Bayesian performance/runtime results. CUB scores and the retained appendix complexity/correlation tables are unchanged.

T1.justification: v5 adds an explicit data-and-knowledge generating model with conditional-independence assumptions, Theorem 1's expected-KL inequality and proof, a strict-inequality proposition and corollary, and further informativeness results (Section 3.2.1 and Appendix A.1). These substantially extend v4's probabilistic motivation and existing ELBO/uncertainty derivations.

C1.justification: The central claim that knowledge-conditioned meta-learning can improve data efficiency remains. v5 narrows the novelty framing from first formalising a general paradigm to offering a perspective on conditional meta-learning, adds theoretical motivation to its stated contributions, and drops the abstract's explicit observational-noise robustness claim.

C2.justification: v5 substantially expands applicability boundaries: ideal-posterior guarantees need not hold for finite learned approximations, semantically novel knowledge entails distribution-shift challenges, and assembling sufficiently varied training tasks can be difficult. Sections 6 and A.8.4 also develop the accuracy, guarantees and computational tradeoffs of learned versus explicit knowledge integration, beyond v4's existing overfitting and spurious-correlation caveats.

D1.justification: v5 Section 7 adds repository and synthetic-data access information, while still deferring image-classification code. It also specifies the two-layer classification decoder, reports manual checking of generated forecasts, and supplies Bayesian sampling settings and training/inference timings. Most existing implementation, hardware and hyperparameter details are retained.

R1.justification: v5 substantially revises positioning by acknowledging conditional meta-learning work by Denevi et al. and the related formulation of Ashman et al. It adds discussion of LLM Processes, Time-LLM and LLM forecasting, replacing v4's separate natural-language-priors discussion and reframing the contribution relative to existing knowledge-integration approaches.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten. v5 reorganises the main argument around a separate problem setting, meta-learning preliminaries, theory and practical considerations, and structures the empirical discussion around explicit questions. The appendices are extensively reorganised and gain a contents table.

P2.justification: v5 changes the main text from two columns to one and substantially redesigns the visual presentation. It adds data-generation and workflow diagrams, splits and recombines experimental panels, restructures the weather and classification tables, and adds analytical displays. Earlier paradigm-comparison and INP architecture diagrams and the averaged-uncertainty plot are removed.

improvement.justification: The clearer formulation, Bayesian-reference analysis, expanded limitations and reproduction access improve the justification and practical calibration of v4's largely illustrative proposal. However, Figure 7b contradicts the retained weather percentages, and Appendix A.1.3's strict-improvement proof relies on positive probability of an empty context without stating that condition in Proposition 1. These issues limit the net quality gain.
